intro: This branch connects math to everyday life: comparing lengths, weights and amounts, telling time, reading a calendar, counting money, and reading simple charts. It shows learners that numbers are useful for describing the world.

I.7.01.what: Comparing how long things are, to say which is longer or shorter.

levels.a: Says which of two things is longer or shorter when their ends line up.
levels.b: Compares lengths whose ends don't line up, by counting grid spaces.
levels.c: Puts three things in order from shortest to longest.
levels.d: Compares two things by checking each against a third, like a piece of string.

I.7.02.what: Measuring length by laying small objects, like paper clips, end to end and counting them.

levels.a: Knows the objects must touch with no gaps or overlaps.
levels.b: Measures something by counting paper clips laid end to end.
levels.c: Counts longer rows of units carefully, counting on from 10.
levels.d: Understands that bigger units give a smaller count for the same length.

I.7.03.what: Using a ruler to measure length in centimeters or inches.

levels.a: Reads a length from a ruler when the object starts at zero.
levels.b: Finds the length when the object doesn't start at zero.
levels.c: Gives a length to the nearest whole centimeter.
levels.d: Works out where to stop to draw a line of a given length.

I.7.04.what: Solving everyday problems about length, and making sensible guesses of how long things are.

levels.a: Adds two lengths together, like a ribbon made longer.
levels.b: Works out how much longer one thing is than another.
levels.c: Picks a sensible estimate for a real object, like a fork being about 18 cm.
levels.d: Measures to check a guess and says how far off it was.
levels.e: Works backwards: knows the whole ribbon and one piece, finds the other piece.
levels.f: Works out every length two sticks can measure, end to end or by their difference.

I.7.05.what: Comparing how heavy things are, using a balance scale or small cubes as weights.

levels.a: Says which of two familiar things is heavier or lighter.
levels.b: Reads a balance scale: the heavier side goes down.
levels.d: Puts three things in order from heaviest to lightest.

I.7.06.what: Comparing how much different containers hold (their capacity), using cups of water.

levels.a: Says which of two containers holds more.
levels.b: Counts how many cups it took to fill a container.
levels.c: Compares two containers by how many cups each holds.
levels.d: Puts three containers in order from holding least to most.

I.7.07.what: Telling time to the hour on a clock with hands and on a digital clock.

levels.a: Knows the short hand is the hour hand.
levels.b: Reads o'clock times from a clock with hands.
levels.c: Matches a digital time like 10:00 to a clock with hands.
levels.d: Picks the clock that shows a given o'clock time.

I.7.08.what: Telling time to the half hour, such as half past 2 or 2:30.

levels.a: Reads half past times when the long hand points to 6.
levels.b: Works out where the long hand should point from where the short hand is.
levels.c: Matches half past times to digital times, like 2:30.
levels.d: Picks the clock that shows a given half past time.

I.7.09.what: Telling time to five minutes, and knowing morning (a.m.) from afternoon or evening (p.m.).

levels.a: Counts by fives around the clock to find the minutes past the hour.
levels.b: Reads any time to five minutes, like 2:45.
levels.c: Reads quarter past and quarter to times.
levels.d: Decides whether a time is a.m. (midnight to noon) or p.m.
levels.e: Works out how many minutes pass between a start time and an end time.
levels.f: Finds the real time from a clock that runs a few minutes fast or slow.

I.7.10.what: Knowing the days of the week and months of the year, and reading a calendar.

levels.a: Knows the order of the days and counts days ahead.
levels.b: Knows the months and facts like how many days are in February.
levels.c: Finds information on a calendar page.
levels.d: Works out dates a few days before or after a given date.
levels.e: Counts on or back several days, as in '5 days ago it was Sunday; what day is today?'
levels.f: Uses the fact that days repeat every 7 to find the weekday of a later date.

I.7.11.what: Recognizing US coins and counting up their value in cents.

levels.a: Names the penny, nickel, dime and quarter.
levels.b: Knows each coin's value, noticing that size doesn't match value.
levels.c: Counts the total of several coins of the same kind.
levels.d: Counts a mix of coins, starting with the biggest.

I.7.12.what: Choosing coins to pay an amount and working out the change.

levels.a: Picks coins that add up to a given amount.
levels.b: Checks whether two different sets of coins make the same amount.
levels.c: Works out change from 10 cents by counting up.
levels.d: Works out change from a dollar, which is 100 cents.
levels.e: Finds the fewest coins that make an amount.
levels.f: Counts every different way to make an amount using 1, 5 and 10 cent coins.

I.7.13.what: Recording and reading counts with tally marks, where every fifth mark crosses a group of four.

levels.a: Counts a small set of tally marks.
levels.b: Reads and makes tallies grouped in fives.
levels.c: Turns a set of votes into a tally chart.
levels.d: Answers questions using a tally chart, such as the total number of votes.

I.7.14.what: Reading and making picture graphs, where each small picture stands for one vote or item.

levels.a: Reads how many chose something by counting pictures in a row.
levels.b: Picks the picture graph that matches a tally chart.
levels.c: Compares rows to find the most or fewest chosen.
levels.d: Works out how many more or fewer one row has than another.

I.7.15.what: Reading and making bar graphs, where the height of each bar shows how many.

levels.a: Reads the value of a bar from the scale beside it.
levels.b: Picks the bar graph that matches a tally chart.
levels.c: Compares bars to find how many more one has than another.
levels.d: Adds bars together to find a total.

I.7.16.what: Asking a question, collecting answers, and showing them on a chart to learn something.

levels.a: Chooses a good survey question, one that gets different answers from different people.
levels.b: Sorts a list of answers into a tally chart.
levels.c: Picks which graph answers a given question.
levels.d: Chooses a true statement about what a graph shows.
